analysis:
Examined base_text units of docs/developer/test.md, base lines 1-939. They contain only test-procedure documentation: SSD test volume, GLM, MiMo, checkpoint storage, endpoint resumption, add-on hold (TB-012/T-059/T-060), App Attest dispatch and native qualification. Per file_changes (range_map_complete=true), the base-side changes are line 3 (date) and lines 1048-1052. Lines 1048-1052 are outside these units. The head-side changes are lines 1048-1059 and 1066-1078, and the patch excerpt is truncated.

The visible patch rewrites the description of scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py. The base said the lane was dispatch-only with a `ref` input and had no signing identity or secret. The head says the lane triggers on push to `dev`, calls release-provider.yml with environment: dev and secrets: inherit, and that its signing job uses five Apple signing secrets plus the Developer ID to sign, notarize and staple. This is documentation only, but it implies a workflow change. The dev lane now appears to inherit the Apple Developer ID signing secrets and produce Developer ID-signed, notarized artifacts from the dev branch.

This could matter for A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034 and T-054. Under those entries, signed-artifact identity is not a serving grant; official-build registration and qualification are separate. Whether dev-branch artifacts can be registered or qualified as official builds depends on the workflow YAML and platform policy, neither of which is supplied. No finding is made, because the workflow source is not in evidence and the changed head lines are not visible in these units.

Integration should check that release-provider.yml with environment: dev cannot reach production publication, and that DEV_RELEASE_KEY gating is preserved. It should also check that Developer ID-signed dev artifacts cannot satisfy official-build registration (T-054) and confirm who can push to `dev`. The threat model may need updating if the signing secrets are newly exposed to the dev branch.
